target_customer: Commercial and institutional satellite operators and agencies that need heavy-lift launch capacity in Europe, booked and paid by the kilogram
problem: Europe has little available or affordable heavy-lift launch capacity, and the company argues Ariane 6 is expensive and scarce.
business_model: Launch services sold per kilogram of payload capacity, with launch reservation agreements as the early commercial instrument
product_category: Reusable heavy-lift launch vehicle and rocket engine

founders.name: Charlie Weise
prior_employers: ESA Argonaut Moon Lander engine work (as described on the YC page)
education: TU Dresden aerospace engineering (per Payload and university coverage)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he worked on a space telescope and the Argonaut lander engine

founders.name: Paul Kunhart
prior_employers: TU Dresden Aerospace Institute (ESA Argonaut nozzle design)
previous_startups: Innuendo (air-breathing cruise missile with rotating detonation engine, outcome not researched)

competitors.name: Isar Aerospace
competitors.what: German orbital launch startup, small-lift Spectrum rocket, reusability as a goal
competitors.traction_then: Spectrum flew in 2025 and again in September 2026 per DLR
competitors.funding_then: EUR 270M raised in June 2026 per a search summary of DLR coverage

competitors.name: Ariane 6
competitors.what: Europe's incumbent heavy launcher that RATLOG hopes to undercut

competitors.name: Rocket Factory Augsburg
competitors.what: German small-lift RFA One, not heavy-lift
competitors.traction_then: ESA European Launcher Challenge contract of EUR 186.9M in Aug 2026 per search summary; first flight not confirmed

technical_complexity.rationale: Orbital-class reusable heavy-lift rocket with a novel engine concept that drops turbopumps. Company reports only a first small hot-fire; a larger engine test was planned for November 2026 and first launch is targeted for 2029 or 2030.

defensibility.rationale: Engine design aiming at about 90 percent fewer parts could be hard to copy if it works, and launch is capital heavy, but nothing is proven at flight scale yet.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Too early to tell; no incumbent response recorded as of November 2026.

market_need_then: European institutional customers lack independent heavy-lift options; company claims over 400 million dollars in launch reservation agreements, which is self-reported and not binding purchase evidence.

identity.visual_style: terse numbered sections, bus to space metaphor

branding.brand_signature: The bus to space framing, capacity sold by the kilogram

brand_strength.rationale: Brand is a few weeks old; sources show a clear metaphor but no press about the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: RATLOG is a Fall 2026 YC company with an active status and no outcome yet. The signals so far are a small German grant, a first hot-fire, and self-reported launch reservations; the long timeline to a 2029 or 2030 launch means capital and technical execution are the main open risks.
notes: Dealroom lists a 125k seed and another page claims 500k via YC; neither confirmed by a second source, so not recorded as rounds. Founded year conflicts: YC page says 2026, one search summary says 2025. Founder education for Weise and Kunhart comes from Payload and university coverage as summarized by search, not opened directly. Outcome search found no shutdown or layoffs. Site claims over 400M dollars in reservation agreements, self-reported.
